rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Newton's three laws run mechanics. **Inertia:** without net external force a body keeps its state — the lurching bus passenger. **Second law:** force is the rate of change of momentum, $\vec F = d\vec p/dt$, defining the newton (1 kg·m/s²) and, at constant mass, $F = ma$. **Third law:** action and reaction are equal, opposite and on different bodies — rocket recoil, walking, gun kick.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - F = ma = dp/dt; 1 N = 1 kg·m/s² - W = mg - Lift: R = m(g ± a) - Smooth incline: a = g sin θ; rough incline: a = g(sin θ − μ cos θ) - Pulley: a = (m₁−m₂)g/(m₁+m₂); T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁+m₂)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Inertial Frame Requirement:** Newton's laws ($F=ma$) hold only in inertial reference frames. In accelerating (non-inertial) frames, a pseudo-force $-ma_{frame}$ must be added to the FBD to make the equations valid.  ·  **FBD Completeness:** The free-body diagram must include *all* forces acting ON the chosen body: weight, normal, friction, tension, applied forces. Forces exerted BY the body on other objects do NOT belong in its FBD.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Always draw the FBD BEFORE writing equations — a wrong diagram guarantees a wrong answer.  ·  Choose one axis along the direction of acceleration — this makes ma appear on only one axis.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Rocket*** — third law at scale: exhaust backward, rocket forward.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Action–reaction pairs vs equilibrium:** action and reaction act on different bodies (never cancel); balanced forces act on the same body (do cancel).  ·  **Mass vs weight:** mass is intrinsic (kg); weight is a force (N) that changes with g — 60 kg weighs 589 N on Earth but ~98 N on the Moon.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Draw free-body diagrams for 10 different mechanical scenarios and write the ΣF = ma equations.  ·  Solve 5 elevator problems computing apparent weight for upward, downward, and free-fall cases.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Inertia stays, F = ma changes, pairs answer."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A 2 kg block on a smooth 30° incline — find its acceleration.** — a = g sin θ = 9.8 × 0.5 = 4.9 m/s² down the plane; the component of weight along the plane drives it.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most-repeated: state the three laws with examples. Learn the lift and incline formulas — they feed numericals.

rows.label: Classified table
rows.text: 2. Newton's Three Laws (NEB 2021, 2022, 2024) · Law | Statement | Example · **First law (inertia)** | A body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless a net external force compels otherwise | A book on a table stays put; passengers lurch forward when a bus brakes · **Second law** | The rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied net force and in its direction: $\vec F = d\vec p/dt = m\vec a$ | Pushing an empty cart…  ·  2.1 Mass vs weight (NEB 2020) · Mass | Weight · Quantity of matter; intrinsic | Gravitational force on the body: $W = mg$ · Scalar; never changes with location | Vector; varies with g (Moon: 1/6) · SI unit: kg | SI unit: N · Measured by a beam balance | Measured by a spring balance

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The third law pairs never cancel:** they act on different bodies — the ground pushes you forward only because you push it backward.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: First law: no net force → no change in velocity (inertia). Second: F = dp/dt = ma; defines the newton. Third: action = −reaction on different bodies.  ·  Mass (kg, invariant) vs weight (W = mg, N, varies with g).  ·  Lift: R = m(g + a) up, m(g − a) down; weightless when a = g downward.  ·  Terminal velocity: drag + upthrust = weight; depends on viscosity, size, density difference.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Astronauts float not because gravity is absent (it is ~90% of surface g at ISS height) but because they are in continuous free fall.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Newton's Laws at Work The three laws are the operating system of mechanics; their applications — frictionless inclines, connected bodies, lifts, mass vs weight — are NEB's most repeated theory questions. This topic states the laws with examples (NEB 2021, 2022, 2024), applies them, and separates mass from weight (NEB 2020).  ·  ## 2. Newton's Three Laws (NEB 2021, 2022, 2024) | Law | Statement | Example | |---|---|---| | **First law (inertia)** | A body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless a net external force compels otherwise | A book on a table stays put; passengers lurch forward when a bus brakes | | **Second law** | The rate of change of momentum is proportional to the…  ·  ## 3. Worked Numericals **Q1 (3m, 2023):** A body of mass 5 kg changes velocity from 2 m/s to 10 m/s in 4 s under constant net force. Find the force. $F = m\Delta v/\Delta t = 5 \times 8/4 = $ **10 N**. **Q2:** A 60 kg person stands in a lift accelerating upward at 2 m/s². Find the normal reaction. $R = m(g + a) = 60(9.8 + 2) = 708$ N — the person feels heavier.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Friction Direction Logic:** Friction always opposes *relative motion or its tendency*. Static friction can act in the direction of motion (e.g., walking forward, car accelerating) — determine direction by asking 'which way would the surface slip without friction?'  ·  Check units: forces in newtons, masses in kg, accelerations in m/s².  ·  Static equilibrium (a = 0) is just ΣF = ma with a = 0 → ΣF = 0 — the same framework.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: NEB frequently asks: 'Draw the free body diagram and find the acceleration' — the FBD itself carries marks.  ·  Note 1: Pay attention to the conditions under which Application of Newton's laws applies  ·  Note 2: Application of Newton's laws connects to multiple other topics in Science
